decisions.reason: As a prominently presented rebranding of an already liked machine, it carries visible commitment, prior acceptance, and little immediate pressure to reverse course.
Its own product page signals a public launch commitment, and a German machinery maker would usually give a newly introduced core machine more time before admitting failure.
Website mention shows lower public commitment than a full standalone launch, but it still fits the firm's core processing-equipment portfolio and early weak results could be treated as temporary.
Even with only limited website emphasis, a stationary electric shredder is close to the firm's main business and recent development spending makes management likely to persist.
This looks like a more niche variant with less visible promotion, so it has a somewhat higher withdrawal risk, but the short time since launch still favors continuation.
A dedicated webpage suggests meaningful investment and public commitment, and management is likely to justify that commitment by keeping the product on the market.
